review_notes:
I read the whole file. I also checked how it relates to Mathlib's `maximalRealSubfield` (in Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/CMField.lean) and to the local `candidateGenusFieldBase` (in Relative/Degree.lean).

`candidateGenusFieldReal` is built directly on Mathlib's `maximalRealSubfield`. It is only re-expressed as an `IntermediateField ℚ` using `Subfield.toIntermediateField`, so it adds no competing concept. The ℚ-membership proof is routine.

The private `candidateGenusFieldRealBaseEquiv` is a proof-local bridge. It identifies the adjoin of the root inside the real candidate with the base inside the full compositum. It is built from `adjoin_map`, `equivMap` and `equivOfEq`. It is private, it is used only for the unramifiedness transfer, and it is not a competing public version of a Mathlib concept.

The other declarations are specific to this construction. `candidateGenusFieldRealBaseRoot`, the degree-two lemma and the existence theorem all concern the chosen root, so none of them has a Mathlib counterpart that is the same concept. I found no independent Mathlib definition that duplicates any of them. I did not make an exhaustive search for generic lifting lemmas that could replace the private equivalence. Any such lemma would be a proof-shortening matter, which the rubric excludes.
